The '''2014–15 Premier League''' (known as the '''[[Barclays]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 23rd season of the [[Premier League]], the top English professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 116th season of top-flight English football overall. The fixtures were announced on 18 June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/jun/fixture-list-for-2014-2015-season-released.html |title=Fixture list for the 2014–15 season released |date=18 June 2014 |work=Premierleague.com |access-date=19 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140622015108/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/jun/fixture-list-for-2014-2015-season-released.html |archive-date=22 June 2014 }}</ref>	
The season started on 16 August 2014 and concluded on 24 May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=When does the 2014/15 season start? |url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/fans/faqs/when-does-2013-14-season-start/ |website=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |access-date=13 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415045835/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/fans/faqs/when-does-2013-14-season-start/ |archive-date=15 April 2014 }}</ref>

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[2013–14 Premier League|2013–14 season]]. [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] entered as the three promoted teams.

On 3 May 2015, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] won the title with three games to spare after a 1–0 home win over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/may/03/premier-league-chelsea-crystal-palace-match-report |title=Chelsea seal Premier League title as Eden Hazard sinks Crystal Palace |date=3 May 2015 |work=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News and Media |access-date=5 May 2015 }}</ref> It was their first league title since 2010, their fourth Premier League title and their fifth English league title overall.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Chelsea 1–0 Crystal Palace |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32471261 |work=BBC Sport |date=3 May 2015 |access-date=4 May 2015 }}</ref> Holders Manchester City eventually finished second, after a short drop to fourth a few weeks before the final match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/10-worst-english-top-flight-title-defences-ever?page=0%2C2 |title=The 10 worst English top-flight title defences ever |date=21 November 2016 |work=[[FourFourTwo]] |publisher=Haymarket |access-date=28 August 2017 |archive-date=27 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170827213813/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/10-worst-english-top-flight-title-defences-ever?page=0%2C2 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] were the first team to be relegated on 9 May 2015 despite beating [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] 1–0, while [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] suffered the same fate after a 6–0 demolition by Manchester City the next day.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32561780 |title=Hull City 0–1 Burnley |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2015 |access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32571671 |title=Manchester City 6–0 Queens Park Rangers |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2015 |access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> Hull City were the third and final team to be relegated after [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] beat [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sport |date=2015-05-24 |title=Jonas Gutierrez on target as Newcastle beat West Ham to send Hull City |url=https://www.sport.es/en/news/premier-league/jonas-gutierrez-on-target-as-4214033 |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=sport |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-05-24 |title=Hull go down, Newcastle survive on final day of drama |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-relegation-idUKKBN0O90OY20150524 |access-date=2023-02-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lang |first=Jack |date=2015-05-24 |title=Premier League final day: The story of Sunday's action |url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/premier-league-final-day-hull-5753387 |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=mirror |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |date=2015-05-24 |title=Newcastle United avoid drop as West Ham's Sam Allardyce is sacked |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/may/24/newcastle-united-avoid-relegation-jonas-gutierrez-west-ham |access-date=2023-02-18 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> They drew 0–0 against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on the final day of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32770866 |title=Hull City 0–0 Manchester United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2015 |access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref>

Manchester City's [[Sergio Agüero]] won the Golden Boot with 26 goals, with his teammate [[Joe Hart]] clinching a record fourth Golden Glove, having kept 14 clean sheets.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/players/4328/Sergio-Agüero/overview |title=Sergio Agüero: Overview |publisher=Premier League |access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/players/3143/Joe-Hart/overview |title=Joe Hart: Overview |publisher=Premier League |access-date=15 December 2017}}</ref> [[Eden Hazard]] and [[José Mourinho]] were named as Player and Manager of the Season respectively.<ref name="AnnualAwards"/>

An independent commission later [[Manchester City F.C. financial breaches scandal|found that Manchester City breached Premier League financial rules]] during this season, part of a pattern of breaches spanning 2009-2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-29 |title=Premier League statement in full as Man City guilty of ‘sham’ deals and other charges |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/man-city-guilty-premier-league-statement-full-charges-b3058442.html |access-date=2026-10-04 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2013–14 Football League Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=The Football League |date=21 April 2014 |title=Cheap England Football Shirts |url=https://cheapfootballshirts.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140421200715/http://www.football-league.co.uk/latestnews/20140421/ups-and-downs_2293301_3748723#selection-703.10-703.21 |archive-date=2014-04-21 |website=Ups and Downs}}</ref> and [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]], returning to the top flight after respective absences of ten years, four years and one year. They replaced [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] and [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], who were relegated to the [[2014–15 Football League Championship|Championship]] after their respective top-flight spells of three years, thirteen years and one year.

|note_res_ELGS=Since winners of the [[2014–15 FA Cup]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], and winners of the [[2014–15 Football League Cup]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], qualified for the Champions League based on league position, the spot awarded to the FA Cup winners ([[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Group stage|Europa League group stage]]) was passed to the sixth-placed team, [[Liverpool F.C|Liverpool]], and the spot awarded to the League Cup winners ([[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|Europa League third qualifying round]]) was passed to the seventh-placed team, [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], since those teams were the first teams in the table not already qualified for any European competition.

|note_res_EL3Q=ELGS

|note_res_EL1Q=England was given an extra qualification berth for the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#First qualifying round|Europa League first qualifying round]] as one of the top three associations in [[UEFA Respect Fair Play ranking]].<ref name="UEFA Fair play">{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.org/social-responsibility/news/newsid=2244170.html|title=Netherlands, England, Ireland get Fair Play bonus|publisher=UEFA|date=8 May 2015|access-date=8 May 2015}}</ref> The spot was given to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] after finishing on top of the Premier League Fair Play table.<ref name="PL Fair play">{{cite web |url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/may/260515-west-ham-top-fair-play-league.html |title=West Ham get UEFA Europa League place after topping Fair Play Table |publisher=Premier League |date=26 May 2015 |access-date=26 May 2015 |archive-date=6 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706015924/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/may/260515-west-ham-top-fair-play-league.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="PL Fair playBBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32889068 |title=West Ham qualify for Europa League through Fair Play system |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2015 |access-date=26 May 2015}}</ref>

}}</onlyinclude>

==Results==
On 3 May 2015, Chelsea beat Crystal Palace 1–0 to secure the Premier League title with three games to play. [[PFA Player of the Year]] winner [[Eden Hazard]] scored the winning goal near the end of the first half, heading in the rebound of his own penalty kick. The win left Chelsea 16 points ahead of Arsenal, which had five games remaining.<ref name=CBC /> Chelsea were atop the standings the entire year, having got off to a good start.<ref name=CBC /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.statto.com/football/teams/chelsea |title=Chelsea 2014–2015 |publisher=statto.com |access-date=7 May 2015 }}</ref> For Chelsea, it was the fourth title in the last eleven years, but first in the last six seasons. It was the fifth title in the club's 110-year history. "We showed absolutely everything since day one, everything football demands from a team," said manager [[José Mourinho]]. "We had fantastic attacking football, we had fantastic domination ... we defended amazingly well."<ref name=CBC>{{cite news|title=Chelsea clinches Premier League title|work=CBC Sports|agency=AP|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/chelsea-clinches-premier-league-title-1.3059208|access-date=5 May 2015|date=3 May 2015}}</ref> It was Mourinho's 22nd career title. He won titles at Chelsea in 2005 and 2006, before being forced out by owner [[Roman Abramovich]], and returning in 2013. [[Diego Costa]] led Chelsea with 20 goals.<ref name=CBC />
